title: Emirate of Nekor
capsule: The Emirate of Nekor was the first autonomous Muslim state in the western Maghreb, founded around 710 by Salih I ibn Mansur through a Umayyad Caliphate grant in the Rif coastal region of present-day Morocco; the Banu Salih dynasty built the capital city of Nekor near the river of the same name around 760–761 and adhered to Maliki Sunni Islam, aligned with the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba. Norse raiders plundered the capital for eight days in 859, and Fatimid forces sacked it twice, in 917 and 934; despite these catastrophes the dynasty reconstituted itself each time. Salihid rule disintegrated around 1015 under pressure from Berber rivals, and Yusuf ibn Tashfin's Almoravid forces destroyed Nekor definitively in 1080–1081, ending the emirate and incorporating the region into the Almoravid empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The emirate's general location in the Rif is attested by Arabic geographers including al-Bakri and Ibn Hawqal, but its territorial extent beyond the Nekor valley is not precisely defined in surviving sources, and its boundaries must be considered approximate.
